title: Regional signal aggregator conflation led to fallback variant throttle — postmortem
creator: Ava Chen
description: On 2025-02-18 a regional routing incident caused sustained SLO violations for customers in EU-west. A buggy aggregation of regional drain signals caused the routing policy evaluator to treat multiple healthy nodes as drained, triggering immediate fallback to a low-capacity model variant. The fallback variant became saturated leading to increased latency, enqueueing, and elevated error rates for ~27 minutes before mitigation.
timeline: 2025-02-18T10:12:00Z - First alert: EU-west p99 latency > 900ms on generation endpoints (pager sent to SRE on-call)
2025-02-18T10:15:00Z - Traffic graphs showed abrupt drop in traffic to standard-tier model variant (v1.3) and simultaneous spike to fallback-small variant (v1.3-quant-short)
2025-02-18T10:17:00Z - On-call confirmed region routing policy had flipped to prefer fallback for ~40% of EU traffic; started mitigation runbook
2025-02-18T10:23:00Z - Emergency rollback: disabled the regional aggregator component (safe-mode) to force policy to consult raw node health signals; traffic started rebalancing
2025-02-18T10:35:00Z - Steady recovery: latency returned to baseline over next 12 minutes; full stabilization by 10:50Z
2025-02-18T11:05:00Z - Post-incident triage call scheduled; initial bug hypothesis: boolean conflation in aggregator caused false-positive drain state
impact: Customer-facing latency and error-rate SLO breaches for EU traffic. Approximately 14 high-volume customers reported degraded generation latency and a small number observed 5xx spike. Incident duration (mitigation to stabilization): ~27 minutes. No data loss or security exposure detected.
root_cause: The regional signal aggregator service incorrectly combined node drain signals using a logical OR across stale and live sources. Because one stale tombstone (stale decommission marker) persisted for a short window after node replacement, the aggregator produced a "region-level drain=true" result even though active capacity was sufficient. The routing policy evaluator prioritized the aggregated region drain flag when making tier/variant selection, causing routing to divert traffic to a low-capacity fallback variant.
contributing_factors: Aggregator logic treated stale tombstones and transient decommission flags equivalently to active drains
No freshness/TTL enforcement for tombstone signals in the aggregator; stale marker lasted ~90s
Routing evaluator had higher precedence for aggregated region flags than instance-level health metrics
Fallback variant lacked adequate headroom and global rate limiting for sudden surges
Insufficient end-to-end fault-injection tests for the routing evaluation path
immediate_mitigations: Disabled regional aggregator (safe-mode) to revert to instance-level health signals
Increased fallback variant concurrency cap and admission control to avoid unbounded enqueueing
Opened temporary firewall to prevent new canary deployments in EU until stabilization
Communication: status page updates and direct Slack notifications to top-tier customers
long_term_actions: ENG-75210: Fix aggregator boolean logic to add signal freshness checks and require quorum for region-level drain decisions
ENG-75300: Change routing precedence so instance-level live health overrides aggregator flags unless aggregator quorum met
ENG-75490: Implement per-variant surge rate-limiter and token-bucket admission to protect small fallback variants
ENG-75520: Add unit + integration tests that inject stale tombstones and validate routing outcomes
ENG-75640: Create a canary and synthetic workload harness for routing policy changes (console-visible)
monitoring_changes: New metric: routing.aggregator.freshness_pct (percentage of signals < TTL) with alert at < 85%
New alert: routing.fallback.overflow when fallback queue depth > 50 for > 2 minutes
Dashboard: 'Routing decision path' tracing view that shows precedence of signals for each decision (added to Console)
SLO: add early-warning rule for p50->p95 slope in region before p99 breach
owners: Miguel Alvarez - incident lead and aggregator hotfix
Priya Kapoor - routing evaluator changes and tests
Samir Patel - fallback capacity controls and admission policies
Ava Chen - postmortem and customer comms
notes: This incident highlights a class of failure where derived signals (aggregates) can amplify transient state into region-wide policy changes. Our routing decision logic needs to be conservative about aggregated inputs and protect small, inexpensive fallback variants from traffic surges. The recommended priority is to ship aggregator safety (ENG-75210) before any further routing experiments in production.

2025-02-19 - Priya Kapoor: Confirmed replay tests show stale-tombstone path producing false positives; adding TTL enforcement to aggregator inputs.
2025-02-20 - Samir Patel: Implemented temporary rate-limiter on fallback variants; added queue-depth alert to runbook.
2025-02-21 - Janelle Ortiz: Dashboard added and linked. We can now trace decision precedence for 95% of production requests.
